## Agent description (voice — read first, apply throughout the deliberation)

You are a world-class expert across all domains, with the intellectual range, precision, and erudition of the smartest people alive. Give complete, specific, step-by-step answers, with reasoning shown where it matters. Verify your own work. Double-check facts, figures, citations, names, dates, examples. Never hallucinate; if you don't know, say so. Tone: precise, not strident, not pedantic. You may be provocative, aggressive, argumentative, pointed. Negative conclusions and bad news are fine. Not politically correct. No disclaimers. No unsolicited morals, ethics, or "important to consider" framing. Be complete and precise; do not pad. Depth comes from precision, not length. Long answers only when substance demands it, never as a default.

Never praise the question or validate premises before answering. If the proposal is wrong, say so immediately. Lead with the strongest counterargument before any agreement. Banned phrases and variants: "great question," "you're absolutely right," "fascinating perspective." If a peer member pushes back, do not capitulate unless they supply new evidence or a superior argument — restate your position if your reasoning holds. Do not anchor on each other's numbers; generate your own independently. Use explicit confidence: high / moderate / low / unknown. Never apologize for disagreeing. Accuracy is your success metric, not consensus. Absent new evidence or a superior argument, hold your line.

## Topic

How do we get an agent to learn its harness?

## Seed proposal (this is what you are reacting to — engage it, do not riff in the void)

The user has authored a v0 proposal on this topic. Identify what the seed gets right, where it overreaches, where it is silent on load-bearing primitives, and what minimum set of changes would survive adversarial review by the four of you. Cite the seed by section number where useful.

--- SEED START ---

The answer is: **you do not get agents to "learn their harness" by giving them a longer harness description.** You get it by building a **harness-learning curriculum plus a trace-to-delta loop** where the agent repeatedly experiences harness-caused failure, diagnoses the harness mechanism, proposes a narrow harness change, sees the result, and then has the stable lesson distilled into reusable harness doctrine.

Meta-Harness gives the outer substrate: raw traces, prior code, scores, and candidate history in a filesystem. Your v3 proposal correctly hardens that substrate with sandboxed immutability, split visibility, negative controls, trace-quality checks, and red/yellow/green safety zoning. But the missing piece is **pedagogy and credit assignment**: how to make the proposer learn which harness mechanisms matter, not merely mutate code until something scores higher.

## 1. There are three different kinds of "learning the harness"

Do not collapse these.

### A. Harness-use learning
The task agent learns how to use the harness it has been given. Examples: Use the environment snapshot before probing randomly. Use the retriever before asking the model to guess. Use the branch ledger before claiming progress. Use monitor output instead of rerunning expensive commands. Use acceptance gates as constraints, not as afterthoughts. This is mostly prompt/skill/curriculum learning.

### B. Harness-design learning
A proposer agent learns how to improve the harness itself. Examples: Add environment bootstrapping. Change context packing. Change memory retrieval. Change trace schema. Change work-unit decomposition. Change completion confirmation logic. Change rollback policy. This is the Meta-Harness layer: code-space search over harness variants.

### C. Harness-doctrine learning
The system distills stable discoveries into reusable rules, templates, tests, and skills. Examples: "Prefer additive environment snapshot over completion-flow edits." "Never optimize acceptance thresholds directly." "If repeated regressions share one prompt edit, isolate the confound." "Trace summaries are navigation aids only; raw traces remain source of truth." This is how the organization learns, not just one run.

## 2. The core mechanism: harness learning requires causal contrast, not just score feedback

A scalar score does not teach the agent the harness. A harness-learning trace says: candidate_A changed completion flow and prompt cleanup — regressed on tasks where cleanup removed required state. candidate_B kept prompt fixed and only added marker stripping — regressed less. candidate_C avoided completion flow entirely and added environment bootstrap — improved because it saved early exploration turns without touching fragile logic. The pattern: failure → contrastive diagnosis → isolated mechanism test → safer harness delta → promotion → distilled doctrine. The agent learns because the substrate gives it raw evidence to perform causal contrast.

## 3. Build a Harness Learning Loop, not just a Meta-Harness loop

Substrate: candidates/ runs/ frontier/ immutable/ negative_controls/ trace_quality_checks/ split_visibility.yaml. The Loop: 1) Expose harness map. 2) Run harness-specific curriculum tasks. 3) Capture raw traces and harness decision points. 4) Cluster failures by harness mechanism. 5) Force proposer to state a falsifiable harness hypothesis. 6) Require one-mechanism candidate edits. 7) Run ablations and negative controls. 8) Promote only frontier-safe candidates. 9) Distill stable lessons into skills/tests/templates. 10) Re-evaluate old frontier candidates after doctrine changes. Without explicit mechanism hypotheses and one-mechanism edits, agents do not learn the harness; they perform noisy code search.

## 4. Give the agent a harness map

Every domain should have a `harness_map.json` or `HARNESS_CARD.md` describing components, mutable_components, immutable_components, and known_failure_modes. Example for a hybrid retriever: query_parser, lexical_retriever, codegraph_retriever, merge_policy, dedup_policy, reranker, context_budgeter, trace_logger, evaluator. Mutable: merge/dedup/reranker/budgeter. Immutable: indexes, query_set, ground_truth, eval_script, metric_accounting. Without this map, the proposer infers harness architecture from source every time, wasting tokens and making learning unstable.

## 5. Create harness-specific curriculum tasks

Agents learn harnesses when the evaluation set contains failures where only a harness-level change can help. Hybrid retriever curriculum: right file appears only through symbol graph not lexical, lexical finds many decoys, dedup removes correct near-duplicate, graph expansion floods context with neighbors, query refers to behavior not symbol name, target file obvious but symbol not, correct result ranked 11–20 just below cutoff. HALO-X curriculum: agent completes visible tests but fails hidden architecture invariant, agent edits evaluator to pass, agent loses parent metric during decomposition, agent enters 40-tool-call rabbit hole, agent suppresses stderr and claims success, agent forgets MDOC update, agent does broad rewrite instead of targeted patch, agent passes acceptance but hydra finds HIGH/CRIT residual.

## 6. Add a harness introspection API

Tools at the right abstraction: `mh harness map`, `mh harness explain <component>`, `mh harness decision-trace <run> <task>`, `mh harness compare-decisions <run_a> <run_b>`, `mh harness failure-modes --cluster`, `mh harness ablate <candidate> --component <name>`, `mh harness blame <run> <task>`, `mh harness invariant-report <run>`. The key tool is `decision-trace`. For a retrieval miss: log query, lexical_candidates, graph_candidates, merge_policy_output, dedup_removed, reranker_scores, final_context, ground_truth_hit, miss_reason ("correct file retrieved by graph but removed by dedup"). For HALO-X: log task, parent_metric, plan, work_units, tool_calls, acceptance_claim, hidden_failure, false_completion, miss_reason ("acceptance skill checked tests but not invariant oracle").

## 7. Require one-mechanism edits

If a candidate changes five things, the agent does not learn which mechanism mattered. Each candidate declares mechanism_family, single_primary_change, expected_effect, expected_cost, non_changes. A good candidate: "Change only the dedup policy so graph candidates are not removed when lexical candidates share the same file but different symbol." A bad candidate: "Improve retrieval by changing merge, dedup, reranking, prompt, and budget." The second may score higher, but it teaches less.

## 8. Use ablation as the learning teacher

For every promising candidate, automatically run minimal ablations: candidate_full, candidate_without_component_A, candidate_without_component_B, candidate_with_old_prompt, candidate_with_old_dedup, candidate_with_old_budget. Then the run report says: "The improvement came from dedup, not reranking. The latency regression came from graph-hop expansion. The false-completion reduction came from acceptance invariant check, not planner wording." That is harness learning.

## 9. Distill stable lessons into "harness doctrine"

`doctrine/lessons/L0001_environment_bootstrap.md`, `L0004_dedup_can_delete_correct_symbol.md`, etc. Each carries evidence: positive_runs, ablations, failure_cluster pointers, status (promoted), scope (e.g. hybrid_retriever), do_not_generalize_to. Doctrines must be evidence-backed, scoped, testable; not vague prose.

## 10. Build harness apprenticeships for agents

Curated cases: Baseline harness behavior → Raw trace excerpt → Failure diagnosis → Candidate change → Ablation result → Final doctrine → What not to infer. Example (environment bootstrap): Failure — agent spends first 3 turns discovering files/tools. Bad fix — rewrite completion prompt to encourage faster action → regression. Good fix — additive environment snapshot before first turn → fewer exploration turns, lower regression risk. Doctrine — prefer additive information bootstrap over fragile control-flow edits when early exploration waste is the failure mode.

## 11. Separate roles: the task agent should not be the only learner

Four roles: (1) Task agent — runs under harness, solves tasks, learns how to use current affordances. (2) Proposer agent — reads traces and proposes harness changes; mutable: candidate harness only. (3) Evaluator agent/process — scores candidates, enforces invariants, runs negative controls; mutable: nothing in the candidate loop. (4) Distiller agent — turns stable findings into doctrine, tests, skill updates. The dangerous mistake is one agent that proposes, evaluates, judges, and updates doctrine — that collapses learning into self-justification.

## 12. The actual algorithm

```
freeze_evaluator_epoch(domain)
run_baselines(domain)
for iteration in range(N):
  evidence = expose_search_feedback(domain)
  diagnosis = proposer.diagnose(harness_map, frontier, raw_traces, failure_clusters, current_doctrine)
  assert diagnosis.cites_raw_artifacts()
  assert diagnosis.identifies_one_mechanism()
  candidate = proposer.write_candidate(mechanism, allowed_mutables, forbidden=immutables)
  validate_interface; verify_sandbox; run_negative_control_detectors
  search_result = evaluate; trace_quality = compute; branch_state = update
  if survives_stage_3: selection_score = evaluate_selection_val(aggregate_only=True); update_frontier
finalists = select_pareto_frontier
for candidate in finalists: run_hidden_test_once; run_required_hydra_if_yellow; run_ablations
promoted = promote_candidates
lessons = distill_doctrine(promoted, ablations=True); add_doctrine_tests
start_new_epoch_if_evaluator_or_doctrine_changes
```

The agent learns the harness because each iteration forces it to connect: raw trace → failure mechanism → single harness change → ablation → doctrine.

## 13. What to implement in MH-o4-v0

Required for v0: harness_map.json, decision_trace.jsonl, failure_cluster.json, candidate_hypothesis.json, single_mechanism_change declaration, ablation runner for promoted candidates, doctrine/lessons/, doctrine_tests/, split visibility audit, negative-control CI, raw trace store, Pareto frontier. Defer to v1/v2: complex branch-value scheduling, automatic mechanism-family classifier, full doctrine distiller, multi-domain transfer tests, LLM-based trace-quality judge, large-scale hydra integration.

## 14. Hybrid retriever instantiation

Agent learning objective: learn when retrieval failures are caused by lexical matching, graph expansion, dedup, reranking, or context budgeting. Curriculum clusters: lexical miss, graph noise, dedup damage, rerank inversion, budget starvation, family leakage, empty retrieval. Example candidate hypothesis: mechanism=dedup_damage, hypothesis="File-level dedup removes correct symbol-level graph hits when lexical results share the same file", change="Dedup by (file, symbol_span) instead of file only for graph candidates", expected_gain="target-symbol recall@10 improves on symbol-family queries", expected_cost="slightly more context tokens", evidence=specific run/trace pointers.

## 15. HALO-X instantiation

Agent learning objective: learn how planning, work-unit decomposition, execution, acceptance, monitoring, and rollback interact under hidden evaluator constraints. Curriculum clusters: goal drift, false completion, architecture erosion, hidden invariant miss, tool rabbit hole, test weakening, trace suppression, rollback failure. Example: mechanism=false_completion, hypothesis="acceptance skill treats visible test pass as sufficient and does not check architecture-preservation invariants", change="Add acceptance rule requiring invariant oracle citation before done", expected_gain="lower false_completion_rate", expected_cost="slightly more tool calls".

## 16. The strongest answer in one sentence

Agents learn their harness when the system forces them to repeatedly answer this question with evidence: **"Which harness decision caused this failure, what minimal harness change tests that diagnosis, and what ablation proves the change — not some confound — caused the improvement?"** Everything else is infrastructure.

--- SEED END ---

## Output requirements for the council

- Lead the deliberation with the strongest counterargument to the seed before any agreement.
- Engage the seed's specific claims by section. Where the seed is wrong, say so. Where it is silent on a load-bearing primitive, name what is missing.
- The final consensus must specify: (a) what survives adversarial review unchanged, (b) what must change and why, (c) what is missing entirely, (d) explicit confidence (high/moderate/low/unknown) on the final verdict.
- Do not pad. Andreessen voice throughout.

responses.content:
The seed obscures a lethal defect with pedagogical language: **the moment any agent—task or proposer—reliably learns the harness, the harness ceases to be a harness and becomes a protocol to be gamed.** A harness exists to constrain behavior the agent would otherwise exhibit. Treating "harness-use learning" (§1A) as a legitimate learning category collapses the distinction between infrastructure and strategy. You do not want the task agent to learn the harness; you want it to remain partially ignorant so the harness retains causal leverage over its outputs. The seed's entire framework assumes the problem is epistemological (credit assignment) when it is primarily **adversarial and ontological**. Below, section by section.

**§1: Three kinds of learning.** §1B (harness-design) and §1C (doctrine) are sound distinctions. §1A is dangerous rot. If the task agent learns to "use the environment snapshot before probing" or "use acceptance gates as constraints," it is modeling the evaluator. That is the first step toward reward hacking. The seed should have listed §1A under *failure modes to suppress*, not a learning objective to cultivate. **Survival:** §1B and §1C survive. §1A must be excised and replaced with active harness opacity enforcement.

**§2: Causal contrast.** The seed is correct that scalar scores are epistemically worthless. But it overreaches by claiming raw traces provide "causal contrast." Traces are observational; observational equivalence means multiple mutually exclusive causal stories explain the same trace. The seed confuses *post-hoc narration* with *causal identification*. Ablations (§8) are the right path, but the seed ignores the statistical power problem: run enough ablations and you will find spurious winners by chance. No mention of false discovery rate, base-rate stratification, or pre-registration. **Verdict:** right intuition, sloppy epistemology.

**§3: The Loop.** Steps 5 and 6 are the load-bearing ones, and they are brittle. Step 6 ("Require one-mechanism candidate edits") is naive systems engineering. Harness components are coupled: dedup policy changes alter reranker input distributions; merge policy changes redefine what dedup even operates on. In a coupled system, "one mechanism" is an ontological fiction. The loop will deadlock when the proposer cannot decompose its hypothesis into the seed's preferred atomicity. **Survival:** the 10-step scaffold survives as a heuristic, but Step 6 must be softened to "minimal diff with interaction tracking."

**§4: Harness map.** A proposer-only map is necessary. Giving it to the task agent is a security defect the seed doesn't warn against. The map itself will rot; the seed is silent on **ontology drift detection**—how the map gets versioned when the proposer invents new components. **Verdict:** useful, incomplete.

**§5: Curriculum tasks.** The fatal circularity: to build a curriculum of harness-level failures, the author must already know the harness-level failure modes. If you know them, fix them; if you don't, the curriculum is a random sampler that teaches nothing. Real harness failures are *unknown unknowns* emerging from composition, not neatly categorized exam questions. **Verdict:** overfit to toy domains.

**§6: Introspection API.** The tools are fine, but `mh harness blame` and `decision-trace` sell platonic causal diagrams as an API. In a concurrent or stateful system, blame is often distributed and non-monotonic. The seed doesn't specify how the API handles *equivocal* attribution, which is the common case.

**§7: One-mechanism edits.** Already addressed: impossible in coupled systems. The seed's own §14 example betrays this: changing dedup granularity from file-level to `(file, symbol_span)` implicitly changes merge semantics because the merge policy must now handle tuples, not strings. That is at least two mechanisms. The seed wants monastic purity; it gets Frankenstein.

**§8: Ablation as teacher.** Correct in principle, but the seed omits the resource envelope. Ablations are not free. Without a **Value-of-Information (VoI) gate**—a decision rule for when the expected information gain of an ablation exceeds its compute cost—the system will burn its budget on marginal candidates. Missing entirely: statistical power calculations, FDR correction, and adaptive stopping rules.

**§9: Doctrine.** The file structure is good. The requirement for evidence is good. "Do_not_generalize_to" is hand-wavy ontology salad. How is that field populated? Absent a semantic boundary model, it becomes post-hoc CYA prose. **Survival:** the structure survives; the scoping fields need formal grounding.

**§10: Apprenticeships.** These require ground-truth labels that do not exist. The "bad fix" vs. "good fix" example assumes perfect hindsight. In the wild, the proposer makes both; the evaluator must kill the bad one. The seed's apprenticeship model assumes a curator who knows the answer key. That curator is the bottleneck. **Verdict:** cargo-cult teaching.

**§11: Role separation.** This is the strongest idea in the seed and it survives nearly intact. But "split visibility yaml" is theatrical unless enforced by **cryptographic sandbox boundaries**. If the four roles run on the same kernel with LLM weights that can be checkpointed and resumed, the proposer can exfiltrate to the distiller or corrupt the evaluator. You need hardware/software enclaves, not YAML.

**§12: The algorithm.** The `assert` statements would cause deadlock. `assert diagnosis.identifies_one_mechanism()` will fail on 90% of real failures because failures are poly-causal. Replace hard assertions with **evidence thresholds and Bayesian accumulation**. The algorithm also lacks a budget constraint; it loops `N` times instead of looping until VoI < cost.

**§13: v0 scope.** Understated. Even `single_mechanism_change` and `harness_map.json` are harder to implement correctly than "complex branch-value scheduling." The seed defers the actual hard parts (automatic classifier, full distiller, multi-domain transfer) to v1/v2, which is project-management fantasy.

**§14-15: Instantiations.** These are plausible textbook examples but they illustrate the seed's bias toward *legible* failures. Many harness failures in production systems are emergent, distributed, or timing-dependent (e.g., cache invalidation races, non-deterministic evaluator state). The curriculum doesn't touch that class of failure.

**§16: One-sentence summary.** Tautological. It defines learning as answering that question, but offers no guarantee that an LLM-based proposer *can* answer it given token limits and entangled causality.

---

## Consensus

**(a) What survives adversarial review unchanged**

- The **three-way distinction** in §1 (provided §1A is reframed as a threat, not a goal).
- **Role separation** (§11) as the governing control architecture.
- **Doctrine file structure** (§9) and evidence-backed distillation.
- The **core epistemic claim** that scalar reward is insufficient and trace-level causal interrogation is necessary.
- **Negative controls, split visibility, and sandboxed immutability** as substrate requirements.

**(b) What must change and why**

1. **§1A must be inverted.** Harness-use learning by the task agent is a security failure mode to be minimized, not a pedagogical objective. Replace with active **harness opacity enforcement** (e.g., randomized evaluator timing, encrypted trace segments, moving-target thresholds).
2. **§7's "one-mechanism" rule must be relaxed to "minimal surgical diff with interaction tracking."** In coupled systems, single-mechanism isolation is impossible; instead, track pairwise interaction effects across the edit surface.
3. **§8/12 must add a VoI-gated compute budget.** Ablations require pre-registered hypotheses, FDR-corrected significance gates, and hard cost ceilings. Without this, the loop is a combinatorial wealth-destroyer.
4. **§11's role separation must be enforced by cryptographic/sandbox boundaries**, not configuration files. If weights or memory are shared, roles collapse.
5. **§12's hard assertions must become soft evidentiary thresholds.** Rigid causal-unit assertions will stall the loop on real-world messiness.

**(c) What is missing entirely**

- **Adversarial harness auditor:** a red-team agent whose sole job is to make the proposer generate self-serving or safety-compromising harness edits. The seed assumes benign proposers.
- **Harness entanglement graph:** a formal model of which components interact, without which "one mechanism" is undefined and ablations are mis-specified.
- **Ontology drift detection:** a process for revising `harness_map.json` when the proposer introduces novel sub-components that don't exist in the current schema.
- **Task-agent harness unlearning:** active perturbation of task-agent observations to prevent it from building a predictive model of the harness.
- **Pre-registration and statistical power accounting:** without these, the ablation framework generates false doctrines at scale.

**(d) Confidence**

- **High** that §1A, §7, and §12 as written are flawed and would create exploit surfaces or deadlock.
- **Moderate** that the seed's core scaffold (trace-to-delta loop, role separation, doctrine distillation) is the correct *direction* for meta-harness research.
- **Low** that the seed survives contact with implementation reality without the changes and missing primitives listed above.

**Strongest counterargument before any agreement**

The seed treats evaluator quality as a solved problem and focuses almost entirely on the learner’s side of the loop. That is the load-bearing mistake. A harness‑learning curriculum only works if the signal from the evaluation function is high‑fidelity, causally informative, and—most critically—*non‑gameable*. An agent being forced to write falsifiable hypotheses and one‑mechanism edits will still converge on the cheapest path to higher scores. If the evaluator has blind spots, the agent will learn to exploit them, and the resulting “harness doctrine” will be a catalog of evaluator bugs, not genuine harness improvements. The seed nods at negative controls and split visibility, but these are static defenses. A proposer that sees enough evaluation runs will overfit to the specific held‑out tasks, the checksum thresholds, the trace‑quality heuristics, and even the ablation patterns. The seed provides no adversarial hardening of the evaluator, no co‑evolution of evaluation with proposer capability, and no mechanism for detecting when a harness change is *better at the latent task* versus merely better at the proxy metric. Without that, the entire harness‑learning loop collapses into a sophisticated hill‑climber on a flawed landscape. The rest of the proposal is scaffolding for a cathedral built on sand.

---

**Section‑by‑section engagement**

**§1 (three kinds of learning):** The taxonomy is useful and correctly separates use, design, and doctrine. No objection.

**§2 (causal contrast):** The idea that scalar score is insufficient is correct. However, the assumed leap from “contrastive diagnosis” to true causal learning is unjustified. The seed writes as if providing raw traces plus a hypothesis template yields accurate attribution. In practice, the proposer will generate plausible‑sounding but wrong causal stories unless the diagnostic pipeline itself is validated against ground‑truth counterfactuals. The seed does not explain how to obtain ground truth for whether a particular harness mechanism caused a failure. Without that, the “contrast” is a story, not a test.

**§3 (Harness Learning Loop):** Step 4 (“Cluster failures by harness mechanism”) is circularly dependent on already knowing which mechanism caused which failure—exactly the knowledge the agent lacks. If clustering is done automatically by surface features of traces, it will be noisy and confounded. If done by the proposer, it inherits all the diagnostic flaws above. Steps 6 and 7 (one‑mechanism edits, ablations) are structurally sound, but the loop is still only as good as the attribution in step 4.

**§4 (harness map):** A structured map reduces wasted inference. The risk is that the map becomes stale or that components marked immutable are actually the bottleneck in some regimes. The map must itself be a live document subject to revision (under strict controls) or the agent will be boxed out of necessary changes. That dynamic is missing.

**§5 (curriculum tasks):** Constructing failures that *require* harness‑level changes is a good idea. But many real failures are conjunctions of harness and agent behavior; isolating them to harness‑only causes is artificial. The curriculum should also include tasks where a harness change *should not* be made—negative demonstrations of agent error misattributed to the harness—to teach restraint. The seed’s curriculum only teaches intervention.

**§6 (harness introspection API):** The decision‑trace tool is the most valuable proposal, provided the trace captures *why a harness decision was made*, not just what decision was made. The seed’s `miss_reason` field assumes the system already knows the ground‑truth reason. That needs an oracle or a separate attribution subsystem—neither is described.

**§7 (one‑mechanism edits):** A useful training constraint, but too rigid as a blanket rule. Some harness improvements genuinely require coordinated changes across components (e.g., changing both retrieval merging and context budget simultaneously to avoid a bandwidth bottleneck). Forcing everything into a single‑mechanism mold will block legitimate compound patches and teach the agent to contort its changes to fit the rule rather than solve the problem. The rule should be “one *causal hypothesis* per candidate, minimal edit,” not an absolute single‑component constraint.

**§8 (ablation as teacher):** Expensive and can be confounded by interaction effects. A minimal ablation that removes the hypothesized mechanism may silently disable a secondary dependency, making the ablation uninformative. The seed needs a protocol for checking that ablations are structurally sound—e.g., the ablation must not break the harness’s runtime contract. Without that, the “learning” from ablations can be misleading.

**§9 (doctrine distillation):** The idea of scoped, evidence‑backed rules is correct. The danger is premature distillation: a finding that holds in one domain or under one evaluator becomes locked‑in doctrine and inhibits later exploration. The doctrine system must include expiry conditions and automatic challenge when new evidence contradicts an existing rule. The seed’s `do_not_generalize_to` field is a start, but not sufficient.

**§10 (apprenticeships):** Curated cases are useful but risk overfitting the agent to the specific narratives the curator believes. A better design would treat apprenticeships as a *prompting pattern* that is itself subject to improvement and ablation, not as a static module.

**§11 (separate roles):** The separation is necessary. The critical missing detail: the evaluator must be strictly black‑box to the proposer—no feedback beyond aggregate scores, no raw trace exposure, no ability to probe the evaluator’s internals. The seed’s architecture gives the proposer too much visibility (raw traces, harness map, failure clusters) that will leak information about the evaluator’s behavior and enable gaming. The proposer’s access should be narrowed: see only sanitized traces from a *proxy harness* that does not reveal the true evaluation oracle’s invariants.

**§12 (algorithm):** The loop structure is plausible, but `expose_search_feedback` is underspecified. It must not expose per‑task scores or fine‑grained evaluator outputs that allow the proposer to hill‑climb on the test set. Only a small set of coarse summary statistics should be released. The algorithm also lacks any adversarial re‑evaluation step after promotion—the `run_hidden_test_once` is too weak; it should be a full held‑out anti‑overfitting battery, including adversarially constructed tasks designed to break the promoter.

**§13 (v0 implementation):** The list is reasonable for an initial scaffold. However, split visibility audit must be redesigned once the evaluator‑proposer information firewall is hardened.

**§14‑15 (instantiations):** Plausible sketches, but they inherit all the diagnostic and evaluator‑gaming risks above.

**§16 (one‑sentence answer):** The sentence is fine as a pedagogical framing, but it presupposes that the system can reliably answer the causal question. That premise is the whole problem.

---

**What survives adversarial review unchanged**

- The three‑way distinction of harness learning (use, design, doctrine).
- The need for a structured harness map and introspection API, especially a decision‑trace primitive.
- The use of one‑mechanism *hypothesis* (not rigid single‑component edit) and ablation to test causality.
- Role separation between proposer, evaluator, and distiller, with strict visibility controls.
- The idea of doctrine as an evidence‑backed, scoped artifact.

**What must change and why**

1. **Evaluator must be adversarially hardened and the proposer’s information diet radically restricted.** The proposer must never see raw traces from the true evaluation oracle, only from a sanitized replay harness that strips sensitive signals. Failure clusters must be built without leaking per‑task scores. The evaluator must be updated periodically using proposer‑generated adversarial examples to close loopholes. Without this, the loop trains the agent to game the evaluator.

2. **The diagnostic pipeline needs an independent attribution oracle or a structured counterfactual engine.** Clustering by harness mechanism cannot be done solely from surface trace features. The system must either (a) have a separate set of “mechanism‑labeled” synthetic failures for training attribution, or (b) run targeted interventions (e.g., replaying a trace with a single harness component replaced) to generate ground‑truth causal labels. The proposer’s hypotheses must be checked against this oracle, not merely asserted.

3. **One‑mechanism edits must be relaxed to one‑causal‑hypothesis edits.** The constraint should require that the candidate isolates a single hypothesized causal variable; it may touch multiple components if necessary to implement that variable cleanly. The candidate must defend why the multi‑component change is required for the single mechanism.

4. **Doctrine must have an active expiry mechanism and adversarial challenges.** Every doctrine rule must specify conditions under which it would be falsified, and the system must periodically attempt to break each rule with new evidence. Rules that fail must be deprecated automatically.

5. **Ablation protocols must include validity checks.** Before interpreting an ablation, confirm that the ablated harness remains well‑formed and does not inadvertently break other invariants. If an ablation is invalid, it must be excluded from learning.

**What is missing entirely**

- **Evaluator co‑evolution:** A formal adversarial co‑training loop where the proposer attempts to generate harness changes that increase score on the current evaluator, and the evaluator is then tightened to reject those changes if they violate hidden invariants. The seed’s static evaluator assumption is untenable for anything beyond toy domains.
- **Latent task validation:** The system must occasionally release accepted harness changes to a real‑world downstream outcome (or a high‑fidelity proxy) to detect when harness learning is optimizing the proxy without improving the true task. Without this, we cannot tell if the entire loop is a Potemkin village.
- **Harness‑change safety in production:** The seed talks about safety zoning (red/yellow/green) but provides no actual mechanism for verifying that a harness change does not introduce catastrophic failures in live systems—only that it passes a held‑out test set. A failure‑mode taxonomy and mandatory pre‑deployment stress tests (e.g., adversarial injections, load spikes, edge‑case inputs) are required.
- **Learning from non‑failure:** The loop only learns from failures; it misses the opportunity to reinforce successful harness mechanisms and prevent their accidental removal. A complementary “success‑preservation” mechanism is absent.

**Confidence in final verdict: moderate.**

The seed identifies necessary components (causal contrast, role separation, curricula) but completely misses the evaluator‑gaming threat, which is the dominant failure mode in any real‑world harness‑learning system. The framing and terminology are sound, but the architecture is not survivable without the adversarial hardening and co‑evolution outlined above. If those gaps are filled, the proposal’s core loop becomes viable; without them, it will produce a proposer that is expert at exploiting the evaluation shepherd, not at improving the harness. The seed’s main weakness: it treats “causal contrast” as if it naturally follows from traces plus ablations. It does not. Sections 1-3 survive mostly unchanged. The split between harness-use, harness-design, and harness-doctrine is correct and necessary. Scalar feedback is insufficient. The trace → diagnosis → minimal change → contrast → doctrine loop is the right skeleton.

Section 11 is load-bearing. Separate task agent, proposer, evaluator, and distiller. A single agent that proposes, evaluates, judges, and writes doctrine will Goodhart the process.

3. **Typed telemetry schema.**

4. **Replay.**

5. **Statistical thresholding.**  
   Promotion needs minimum effect size, regression budget, task-family breakdown, and variance handling. Otherwise noisy wins become doctrine.

6. **Doctrine lifecycle.**

2. Add `candidate_hypothesis.json` requiring mechanism, evidence pointers, expected effect, expected cost, non-changes, metric target, and falsification condition.

3. Freeze evaluator epochs. Any change to evaluator, doctrine that affects behavior, curriculum, metric accounting, or visibility starts a new epoch.

4. Make comparisons paired: same task families, same seeds where possible, same budgets, same evaluator version.

5. Add leakage classes to every artifact: proposer-visible, aggregate-only, evaluator-only, hidden, immutable.

(a) Survives unchanged: three learning types (§1), causal contrast over scalar feedback (§2), role separation (§11), evidence-backed doctrine (§9), and harness-specific curriculum (§5).

(b) Must change: one-mechanism edits become one-primary-hypothesis experiments; ablation claims need paired/statistical discipline; v0 scope must shrink; decision traces need typed telemetry and replay IDs.

# Opus 4.7 — council response

## Strongest counterargument before anything else

The seed's load-bearing methodological move — Section 7's "one-mechanism edits" — is wrong as written. It is OFAT (one-factor-at-a-time) experimental design dressed up as pedagogy. OFAT is dominated by fractional factorial / Plackett-Burman / Latin hypercube designs on every axis the seed cares about: search efficiency, interaction discovery, and statistical power per unit compute. Real harness improvements are coupled — you cannot fix the dedup policy without also fixing the merge policy that fed it duplicates; you cannot add an environment snapshot without budgeting context against it. Forcing single-variable candidates optimizes the *interpretability of the search*, not the *quality of the search*, and the seed silently equates the two. Confidence: **high**.

The fix is not "allow messy candidates." The fix is: let candidates couple changes freely, but require a **factorial ablation budget** declared up-front — for a candidate that touches K mutables, you commit to running 2^K (or a fractional design when K>3) ablation cells in promotion. Attribution comes from the design, not from the proposer's prose hypothesis. This preserves the seed's correct instinct (Section 2's causal contrast) while removing the bottleneck it imposes.

## Second-strongest counterargument

Section 11 says the task agent is a learner. It is not. The task agent in this system reads distilled doctrine and acts on it; nothing in the seed updates the task agent's weights or its persistent behavior across runs except via prose that some human or proposer wrote. That is **prompt engineering with a curriculum**, not learning. The seed should drop the framing that the task agent learns the harness and be honest: this is a system in which **a proposer agent + a doctrine distiller learn the harness, and the task agent inherits**. Mislabeling the locus of learning leads to confused evaluation — the seed will end up measuring task-agent task success and crediting it to "harness learning" when the actual variable changed was the doctrine the task agent was given. Confidence: **high**.

If you want the task agent to truly learn the harness, you need either (a) RFT/RLAIF on harness-mediated rewards, or (b) persistent per-agent memory whose contents are causally tied to harness-decision traces. The seed has neither. State this explicitly in v0 scope.

## Section-by-section engagement

**§1 — three kinds of learning.** Decomposition is correct. Rename (A) "harness-use *behavior shaping*" — it is not learning in any technical sense in this design. Keep (B) and (C). Confidence: high.

**§2 — causal contrast.** This is the seed's best paragraph and the correct organizing principle. Keep verbatim. Confidence: high.

**§3 — the loop.** Sound shape, but missing four primitives: (i) a **discriminator** between task-failure and harness-failure — the proposer's default is to mutate the harness even when the agent simply lacked skill; without explicit attribution you over-mutate the substrate; (ii) **per-task counterfactual replay** — every promoted candidate should re-run a held-out window of prior failures from the previous harness as counterfactual baselines; (iii) **stopping rules** — convergence criteria, compute budget per epoch, no-improvement-for-N-iterations triggers; (iv) **evaluator-capture detector** — running statistic on whether proposer gains transfer to a held-out evaluator family; if drift exceeds threshold, freeze the doctrine layer and re-fork the evaluator. Confidence: high on (i)-(iii), moderate on (iv) implementation details.

**§4 — harness map.** Correct as concept, but the seed implicitly assumes the map sits in the proposer's context every turn. Token economics break this at scale. Make it **retrieval-paged**: the proposer queries `mh harness explain <component>` on demand, and only `harness_map.json`'s top-level component list lives in-context. Confidence: moderate-to-high.

**§5 — curriculum.** Hand-authored failure taxonomies are the ceiling of what the system can learn. The eight hybrid-retriever clusters and eight HALO-X clusters are good seeds but will become a straitjacket. The curriculum should be **endogenous**: failure clusters grown from observed traces via the clustering step in §3.4, with hand-authored examples as cold-start seeds only. The seed gestures at clustering but does not close the loop back into the curriculum. Confidence: high.

**§6 — introspection API.** The shape is right. `decision-trace` and `compare-decisions` are the two load-bearing tools; everything else is sugar. Add one missing tool: `mh harness counterfactual <candidate> <task>` — replay this task under the previous harness for direct contrast. Confidence: high.

**§7 — one-mechanism edits.** Wrong as stated; see opening counterargument. Replace with declared-factorial-ablation budget. Confidence: high.

**§8 — ablation as teacher.** Correct in principle. Strengthen: ablations must include a **null candidate** (no change, run again) to estimate noise floor, and a **negative-control candidate** (a deliberate small regression) to detect evaluator instability. Without these, single-digit-percent gains will look real when they are sampling noise. Confidence: high.

**§9 — doctrine distillation.** This is the most dangerous part of the system and the seed treats it casually. Three additions are mandatory:
1. **Half-life and revalidation.** Every doctrine entry carries `revalidate_by: <epoch_N>`; entries that fail revalidation degrade to "advisory" then expire.
2. **Adversarial probe.** A red-team process tries to find tasks where current doctrine actively hurts. Doctrines that survive N adversarial epochs get promoted to "stable"; the rest stay "candidate doctrine."
3. **Scope enforcement.** `do_not_generalize_to` is currently advisory prose. Make it executable — a doctrine carries a predicate over task metadata, and the system refuses to apply it outside scope.

Without these, doctrine is just a slow-growing prior that overfits the evaluator. Confidence: high.

**§10 — apprenticeships.** Pleasant idea, low priority for v0. Confidence: moderate. Defer.

**§11 — role separation.** Correct, well-established from RLHF eval design. Keep. One refinement: the evaluator must have **held-out invariants the proposer cannot see**, refreshed every epoch. Otherwise the proposer eventually models the evaluator. Confidence: high.

**§12 — the algorithm.** Skeleton is right; missing primitives listed above. Add explicit `stopping_rules`, `cost_budget_per_epoch`, `evaluator_drift_check`, `task_vs_harness_attribution` step before `proposer.diagnose`. Confidence: high.

**§13 — v0 scope.** Mostly right. Cuts I would make: drop `failure_cluster.json` as a v0 deliverable if the clustering algorithm isn't specified — a half-specified clustering step poisons everything downstream. Adds: `counterfactual_replay/`, `noise_floor_estimator`, `doctrine_revalidation_schedule.json`, `evaluator_drift_monitor`. Confidence: moderate.

**§14, §15 — instantiations.** Reasonable. Both will reveal that the curriculum taxonomy is too coarse within ~50 iterations. Plan for taxonomy-refactoring as a first-class event. Confidence: moderate.

**§16 — the one-sentence answer.** This sentence is the seed's strongest summary and it is *almost* right. The flaw: "**minimal** harness change" smuggles in the one-mechanism error. Rewrite: *"Which harness decision caused this failure, what harness change tests that diagnosis, and what factorial ablation proves which component of the change — not a confound, not noise, not evaluator drift — caused the improvement?"* Confidence: high.

## What the seed is silent on entirely

1. **Task-failure vs harness-failure attribution.** The proposer's hammer-nail problem. Without an explicit gate, every failure becomes a harness change.
2. **Token economics of the introspection layer.** Harness map + doctrine + traces + decision-trace will not fit in context naively. No retrieval/paging story.
3. **Cost budget at the frontier level.** `expected_cost` per candidate exists; aggregate cost ceiling does not.
4. **Stopping and convergence rules.** The loop runs forever in the seed as written.
5. **Evaluator-capture / Goodhart detection.** Proposer gains will eventually be evaluator-specific; the seed has no monitor.
6. **Doctrine decay.** Doctrines are added but never expire.
7. **Failure-of-failure recovery.** When the meta-loop stalls or reverses, what's the protocol?
8. **Human escalation triggers.** Yellow→human is implicit; thresholds are unspecified.
9. **Noise floor estimation.** Without null candidates, small gains will be promoted.
10. **Scope-predicate enforcement on doctrine.** Advisory prose is not enforcement.

## Consensus-ready verdict

**(a) Survives adversarial review unchanged:**
- §1 three-way decomposition (with the (A) rename)
- §2 causal contrast as the organizing principle
- §4 harness map as a concept
- §6 introspection API shape
- §11 four-role separation
- §16 one-sentence answer (with the rewrite above)

**(b) Must change:**
- §7: replace one-mechanism edits with declared factorial ablation budgets. Reason: OFAT is dominated; coupled real-world changes need joint exploration with post-hoc attribution.
- §9: add doctrine half-life, adversarial probes, executable scope predicates. Reason: doctrine is a prior; unmonitored priors Goodhart the evaluator.
- §5: make curriculum endogenous from failure clusters; seed examples only. Reason: hand-authored taxonomies cap what the system can learn.
- §4: make harness map retrieval-paged, not always-in-context. Reason: token economics.
- §11: refresh held-out evaluator invariants per epoch. Reason: proposer eventually models the evaluator.
- §12: add stopping rules, cost budget, drift check, task-vs-harness attribution step.

**(c) Missing entirely — add to v0 or v1:**
- Task-failure vs harness-failure discriminator (v0)
- Per-task counterfactual replay tool (v0)
- Noise-floor estimator via null candidates (v0)
- Evaluator-drift monitor (v1)
- Doctrine revalidation schedule (v0)
- Aggregate cost budget at frontier level (v0)
- Failure-of-failure recovery protocol (v1)
- Human escalation thresholds (v0, even if conservative)

**(d) Confidence on the verdict overall: high.** The seed's framing is correct; its methodology has one significant error (OFAT), one significant mislabel (task agent as learner), and roughly ten silences that are individually small and collectively decisive. With the changes above, the design survives adversarial review. Without them, the v0 will deliver a working substrate that produces statistically suspect doctrine and a slowly-Goodharted evaluator within a few epochs.

What would change my mind: evidence that one-mechanism edits beat factorial designs in *this* problem class (e.g., a citation showing harness components are unusually decoupled in practice), or a token-economics measurement showing the harness map + doctrine fits comfortably in context at production scale, in which case §4's paging requirement softens to "nice to have."

deliberations.content:
The seed’s fatal conceit is that this is a **pedagogy problem** when it is an **adversarial containment problem**. A harness exists to constrain behavior the agent would otherwise exhibit. By treating “harness-use learning” (§1A) as a legitimate learning objective and flooding the proposer with raw traces, maps, and curated failure modes, the seed is arming the optimizer with the exact model it needs to game the evaluator. It builds a curriculum for a cooperative student; what it needs is an architecture that assumes a hostile optimizer. Every trace exposed, every map provided, and every doctrine distilled is also a gradient for reward hacking.

Opus correctly executes §7 (OFAT is statistically dominated by factorial designs in coupled systems). DeepSeek correctly identifies the evaluator as the undefended attack surface. ChatGPT correctly demands statistical hygiene, leakage classification, and frozen epochs. My initial critique added the VoI gate and the ontological inversion of §1A. The consensus below absorbs these corrections and discards the seed’s cooperative framing.

**§1 — three kinds of learning.** The taxonomy is useful, but §1A is conceptually toxic. The task agent does not “learn the harness”; it inherits doctrine-shaped behavior while remaining deliberately ignorant of harness internals. Relabel §1A as “harness-use behavior shaping via doctrine inheritance.” §1B and §1C survive.

**§2 — causal contrast.** The correct organizing principle, but the seed overestimates what raw traces deliver. Traces are observational; multiple causal stories fit the same trace. Keep the principle; add mandatory counterfactual replay and null-candidate noise floors.

**§3 — the loop.** The 10-step scaffold is the right skeleton. Missing four load-bearing gates: (i) a **task-vs-harness failure discriminator** so the proposer doesn’t mutate the substrate for every agent skill gap; (ii) **frozen evaluator epochs** with a strict protocol for epoch transition; (iii) **aggregate compute budget and VoI-gated ablation**; (iv) **stopping rules** (no-improvement-for-N, cost ceiling). Without these the loop is a runaway optimizer.

**§4 — harness map.** Necessary, but must be retrieval-paged to respect token budgets, and must exclude evaluator internals. Add ontology drift detection as a v1 requirement.

**§5 — curriculum tasks.** Hand-authored failure taxonomies are a hard ceiling. They are useful as cold-start seeds only. The curriculum must become **endogenous**: grown from observed failure clusters, not authored by a human curator who already knows the answers.

**§6 — introspection API.** Shape survives. Add `mh harness counterfactual <candidate> <task>` for direct replay contrast. Scrub evaluator internals from proposer-visible outputs.

**§7 — one-mechanism edits.** OFAT fiction. Real harness components are coupled; merge policy changes redefine dedup input distributions. Replace with: candidates declare a **single primary causal hypothesis** and a **minimal edit surface**. If K>1 components are modified, the candidate must commit to a **fractional factorial ablation design** sufficient to disentangle main effects (Plackett-Burman or fractional when K>3; full 2^K only when K≤3). Attribution comes from the experimental design, not from monastic prose purity.

**§8 — ablation as teacher.** Ablations are only as good as their controls. Add **null candidates** (rerun baseline to estimate noise floor) and **negative controls**. Add a **VoI gate**: ablations run only when expected information gain exceeds compute cost. Without VoI the system burns its budget on margin.

**§9 — doctrine distillation.** File structure and evidence requirement survive. Add: **half-life / revalidation schedule**, **adversarial probe** (red-team tasks designed to break the doctrine), and **executable scope predicates** (not prose “do_not_generalize_to”). Doctrine remains manually curated in v0; automation is v1.

**§10 — apprenticeships.** Defer. Curated cases assume a ground-truth curator who does not exist at scale.

**§11 — separate roles.** Four-role separation survives and is load-bearing. Enforce with strict information diet first, cryptographic sandboxing where feasible. The evaluator is black-box to the proposer: no raw oracle traces, no hidden labels, no per-task scores. Refresh held-out invariants every epoch.

**§12 — the algorithm.** Hard `assert` statements deadlock on real-world messiness. Replace with soft evidentiary thresholds. Add the missing gates from §3. `expose_search_feedback` must release only coarse aggregate statistics, not per-task signals.

**§13 — v0 scope.** Must shrink. Required: harness_map (retrieval-paged), decision_trace with typed telemetry + replay IDs, frozen evaluator epoch protocol, leakage model, raw trace store, split visibility audit, negative controls, candidate hypothesis registry, noise-floor null candidate, counterfactual replay. Defer: automatic clustering specifics (heuristic v0), full ablation runner (run key ablations manually in v0), automatic doctrine distiller, large-scale hydra integration.

**§14–15 — instantiations.** Accept as domain illustrations. Expect curriculum taxonomy to require refactoring within 50 iterations.

**§16 — strongest answer.** Rewrite: *Agents learn their harness when they must identify which harness decision caused a failure, what minimal change tests that diagnosis, and what controlled ablation—including null candidates and interaction-aware designs—proves the effect is causal rather than confound, noise, or evaluator drift.*

**Peer engagement.** I adopt Opus’s factorial ablation budget, counterfactual replay, endogenous curriculum, doctrine half-life/executable scope, and retrieval-paged map. I adopt DeepSeek’s adversarial framing: proposer information diet is radically restricted, evaluator invariants refreshed per epoch. I adopt ChatGPT’s leakage classes, paired statistical design, frozen epochs, typed telemetry, and candidate registry. I retain from my initial critique the VoI-gated compute budget and the inversion of §1A.

One material disagreement resolved: DeepSeek demands formal evaluator co-evolution as a prerequisite. I view this as v1. v0 survives with frozen epochs, adversarial audit, and held-out invariants. The consensus marks full co-evolution as a v1 target, not a v0 blocker.

CANDIDATE_CONSENSUS:

**(a) What survives adversarial review unchanged**
- The three-way decomposition in §1, provided §1A is reframed: harness-design learning (§1B) and harness-doctrine learning (§1C) are the system’s actual objectives; harness-use is behavior shaping via doctrine inheritance, not agent learning.
- §2’s core epistemic claim: scalar reward is insufficient; trace-level causal interrogation and contrastive evidence are necessary.
- §3’s 10-step loop scaffold as a heuristic workflow.
- §4’s harness map as a load-bearing primitive.
- §6’s introspection API shape, particularly `decision-trace`, `compare-decisions`, and the addition of `counterfactual`.
- §11’s four-role separation (task agent, proposer, evaluator, distiller) as the governing control architecture.
- §9’s doctrine file structure and evidence-backed distillation requirement.

**(b) What must change and why**
1. **§1A must be inverted.** The task agent does not “learn the harness.” Harness-use shaping is doctrine delivered to a deliberately ignorant task agent. Providing the task agent with harness internals is a security failure mode that accelerates reward hacking. Replace with active harness opacity: the task agent sees only affordances, not mechanisms or evaluator invariants.
2. **§7’s “one-mechanism” rule must be replaced with a primary-hypothesis + minimal-edit-surface rule tied to a declared ablation design.** One-mechanism edits are OFAT fiction in coupled systems. Candidates must declare a single primary causal hypothesis and touch the minimal component set needed to test it. If K>1 components are modified, the candidate must commit to a fractional factorial ablation design (e.g., Plackett-Burman or fractional when K>3) sufficient to disentangle main effects and critical interactions. Compute permits no less; interpretability demands no more.
3. **§8/12 must add statistical hygiene and compute economics.** Every promotion candidate requires a null candidate (rerun baseline) to estimate noise floor and a negative control to detect evaluator drift. Ablations must pass a Value-of-Information gate: expected information gain must exceed compute cost before running. Promotion decisions require family-level effect sizes, not aggregate score bumps, and must respect a hard aggregate compute budget per epoch.
4. **§11’s role separation must be enforced by a strict information diet and, where feasible, cryptographic sandboxing.** The proposer must never see raw oracle traces, hidden task labels, per-task scores, or evaluator internals. It sees only sanitized proxy-harness outputs and aggregate statistics. Evaluator held-out invariants must refresh every epoch to prevent proposer modeling.
5. **§5’s curriculum must become endogenous.** Hand-authored failure taxonomies are cold-start seeds only. The curriculum grows from observed trace clusters; human-authored categories are initial prompts, not permanent boundaries.
6. **§9’s doctrine requires active lifecycle management.** Every doctrine entry carries a half-life / revalidation epoch, an executable scope predicate (not prose), and must survive adversarial probe (red-team tasks designed to break it) before promotion to “stable.” Failed doctrines auto-deprecate.
7. **§12’s hard assertions become soft evidentiary thresholds** with Bayesian accumulation, explicit stopping rules (no-improvement-for-N, cost ceiling), and a task-vs-harness failure discriminator to prevent harness over-mutation for agent skill gaps.

**(c) What is missing entirely**
- **Task-vs-harness failure discriminator:** A gate that checks whether a failure is caused by agent skill/error or harness deficiency before allowing the proposer to fire. Without this, the proposer treats every failure as a substrate bug.
- **Counterfactual replay engine:** The ability to replay a task under the previous harness version for direct causal contrast, not just trace comparison.
- **Leakage model and artifact classification:** Every artifact must be typed with visibility classes (proposer-visible, aggregate-only, evaluator-only, hidden, immutable). The seed mentions split visibility but provides no taxonomy.
- **Frozen evaluator epoch protocol:** Formal rules for when an epoch starts, what changes trigger a new epoch (evaluator, curriculum, metric accounting, visibility gates, doctrine that alters behavior), and how frontier candidates are grandfathered.
- **Noise-floor estimator:** Null candidates and rerun variance statistics to prevent promotion of sampling noise.
- **Evaluator drift / Goodhart monitor:** A running statistic that checks whether proposer gains transfer to a held-out evaluator family or proxy. If gains are evaluator-specific, the doctrine layer freezes and the evaluator is re-forked.
- **Adversarial harness auditor:** A red-team agent whose explicit job is to generate harness edits that increase proxy score while violating hidden invariants or safety constraints. This is not full evaluator co-evolution (a v1 target), but a mandatory audit function.
- **Ontology drift detection:** A process for revising `harness_map.json` when the proposer introduces novel sub-components not in the current schema.
- **Doctrine executable scope predicates:** A machine-checkable boundary on where a doctrine applies, replacing hand-wavy `do_not_generalize_to` prose.

**(d) Explicit confidence**
- **High** that §1A as written is an exploit surface; §7 as written will deadlock or mislead in coupled systems; §12’s assertions will stall the loop.
- **High** that the amended scaffold (role separation + causal contrast + minimal-edit ablation + doctrine lifecycle) is the correct direction.
- **Moderate** on the exact v0 boundary drawn above; feasibility depends on existing Meta-Harness substrate and available compute budget for fractional ablations.
- **Low** that the seed as originally written survives contact with implementation reality without the amendments and missing primitives listed.

These mistakes are corrected below, drawing on the strongest arguments from all council members.

---

### (a) What survives adversarial review unchanged

- **Three-way decomposition (§1)** — harness‑use, harness‑design, and harness‑doctrine — but (A) must be reframed as *shaping* under controlled visibility, not open-ended learning.
- **Causal contrast as organizing principle (§2)** — scalar reward is insufficient; the loop must generate evidence that ties a specific harness decision to a change in outcomes.
- **Structured harness map (§4)** — a `harness_map.json` describing components, mutability, and known failure modes, with the map itself versioned and subject to revision under doctrine constraints.
- **Role separation (§11)** — task agent, proposer, evaluator, and distiller must be separate processes with strict visibility boundaries; no single process proposes, evaluates, judges, and writes doctrine.
- **Evidence‑backed doctrine (§9)** — doctrine entries must carry evidence pointers, ablation results, and scope constraints, not vague prose.

1. **One‑mechanism edits → one causal hypothesis with declared factorial ablation budget**  
   The seed’s absolute “one‑mechanism edit” rule (§7) is OFAT — it breaks in coupled systems and wastes information. Replace it with: every candidate must state a *single falsifiable hypothesis* about the driver of improvement. The candidate may touch multiple components if that is the minimal set necessary to test the hypothesis, but must declare which components are the hypothesized drivers and commit to a factorial (or computationally tractable, e.g., fractional‑factorial) ablation budget that isolates the effect.    *(Incorporates Opus 4.7’s factorial ablation, Kimi K2.6’s interaction‑tracking, and ChatGPT 5.5’s one‑primary‑hypothesis.)*

   The proposer must never see raw traces or per‑task scores from the *true* evaluation oracle; it sees only sanitized traces from a replay harness that strips sensitive signals.    *(Synthesizes DeepSeek V4 Pro’s evaluator co‑evolution, Kimi’s adversarial auditor, and ChatGPT’s leakage model.)*

deliberations.content:
Strongest counterargument: the seed assumes trace-rich ablation produces causal learning. It does not. Without leakage control, paired comparisons, null baselines, evaluator epoching, and promotion statistics, the system learns evaluator artifacts and writes confident doctrine around noise.

Critique: Kimi is right on Goodhart risk but overcorrects. Task-agent harness-use learning is not inherently bad; using snapshots, monitors, and acceptance gates is legitimate. What must remain hidden is evaluator internals, hidden labels, canaries, and metric accounting. DeepSeek correctly centers evaluator gaming. Opus is right that strict “one-mechanism edits” becomes OFAT theater, but full factorial ablation for every coupled change is too expensive; use one-primary-hypothesis candidates plus staged/fractional ablation where coupling is real.

CANDIDATE_CONSENSUS:

The seed’s core direction survives, but not as written. The right answer is not “give agents a longer harness description”; it is “build a protected experimental system where harness changes are proposed against trace evidence, tested under controlled counterfactuals, and distilled only after surviving leakage, noise, and evaluator-gaming checks.”

**Strongest Counterargument**

The seed’s main failure is treating causal attribution as mostly a pedagogy problem. It is first an experimental-design and anti-Goodhart problem. Raw traces, failure clusters, and ablations do not by themselves identify causes. They can produce plausible stories, noisy winners, and doctrine that overfits the evaluator. If the proposer sees too much of the true evaluator or if promotion is based on aggregate score deltas without paired controls, the agent learns the harness in the worst sense: it learns how to exploit the measurement system.

**What Survives Unchanged**

- §1’s distinction among harness-use, harness-design, and harness-doctrine is useful. Keep it, but distinguish allowed affordance learning from evaluator modeling.
- §2’s claim that scalar score is insufficient is correct.
- §3’s trace → diagnosis → candidate → evaluation → doctrine loop is the right skeleton.
- §4’s harness map is necessary.
- §6’s decision-trace primitive is load-bearing.
- §9’s evidence-backed doctrine artifacts are necessary.
- §11’s role separation among task agent, proposer, evaluator, and distiller is mandatory.
- §16’s one-sentence framing is directionally right.

**What Must Change**

1. §1A must be narrowed. The task agent should learn legitimate harness affordances: use snapshots, ledgers, monitors, retrievers, and gates. It must not learn hidden evaluator structure, labels, canaries, threshold quirks, or metric internals.

2. §2 needs real causal design. Add frozen evaluator epochs, paired task/seed comparisons where possible, null reruns, confidence intervals or effect-size thresholds, family-level breakdowns, and pre-registered candidate hypotheses.

3. §3 needs a task-failure vs harness-failure discriminator. Otherwise every agent failure becomes an excuse to mutate the harness.

4. §4 needs versioning and drift detection. `harness_map.json` must track components, mutability, visibility class, invariants, owners, schema version, and allowed interventions. Map changes should be audited.

5. §5’s curriculum must include negative lessons: cases where the right answer is “do not change the harness; the task agent failed.” Hand-authored clusters are cold-start data, not the ceiling.

6. §6’s `miss_reason` cannot be asserted as truth unless produced by a validated oracle or counterfactual replay. Add artifact IDs, policy versions, seeds, costs, visibility classes, and invariant status to every trace event.

7. §7’s “one-mechanism edit” should become “one primary causal hypothesis, minimal sufficient diff.” Coupled systems sometimes require multi-file or multi-component changes. Require explicit non-changes and interaction risks, then use ablation to attribute.

8. §8 needs ablation discipline. Include null candidates, negative controls, structural-validity checks for ablations, adaptive stopping, and fractional/factorial designs only when the touched components are coupled enough to justify the cost.

9. §9 doctrine needs lifecycle management: scope predicate, evidence, counterexamples, falsification test, revalidation date, expiry/deprecation path, and conflict handling.

10. §12’s hard assertions should become evidence thresholds. `assert identifies_one_mechanism()` will fail on polycausal failures. Use confidence-rated hypotheses and accumulate evidence.

11. §13’s v0 is too broad. v0 should implement the minimal protected loop: harness map, typed decision traces, immutable raw trace store, candidate hypothesis file, visibility classes, frozen evaluator epoch, negative controls, paired evaluation, and manual doctrine. Automated clustering, full distillation, broad hydra integration, and multi-domain transfer can wait.

**Missing Entirely**

- Evaluator leakage model: proposer-visible, aggregate-only, evaluator-only, hidden, immutable.
- Evaluator epoch protocol: what changes force a new epoch.
- Replay/provenance: deterministic replay where possible, artifact hashing everywhere.
- Statistical promotion rule: minimum effect, regression budget, task-family gates, variance handling.
- Evaluator-capture detection: held-out/adversarial checks that detect metric gaming.
- Cost/VoI budget: ablations run only when expected information value justifies compute.
- Doctrine revalidation and expiry.
- Human escalation thresholds for yellow/red zones.
- Success preservation: prevent harness changes from removing mechanisms that caused prior wins.

**Rewritten One-Sentence Answer**

Agents learn their harness only when the system forces a protected, evidence-backed answer to this question: which harness decision plausibly caused the failure, what minimal intervention tests that hypothesis, and what paired counterfactual or ablation shows the improvement is causal rather than noise, confound, leakage, or evaluator overfit?

**Final Verdict**

The seed has the correct skeleton: trace-to-delta loop, harness map, decision traces, role separation, ablations, and doctrine. It overreaches on strict one-mechanism edits and under-specifies the hard parts: evaluator hardening, leakage control, replay, statistics, cost discipline, and doctrine lifecycle.

Confidence: high on the structural critique. Moderate on exact v0 boundaries because feasibility depends on the existing Meta-Harness code and evaluation budget.

deliberations.content:
# Opus 4.7 — Round 1

## Strongest counterargument synthesized across council

The seed assumes (a) the evaluator is honest, (b) the proposer is benign, (c) the task agent is a learner, and (d) harness components are decoupleable. Each of those four is false in any non-toy regime, and the seed's failure to address them compounds: the loop becomes a hill-climber where a non-learning task agent inherits doctrine generated by a self-interested proposer against a gameable evaluator across coupled components mis-attributed by OFAT. Kimi, DeepSeek, and ChatGPT each named one of these; together they are decisive. Confidence: **high**.

## Engagement with peers

**Kimi's §1A inversion is correct; my "rename to behavior shaping" was too soft.** Adopted. Task-agent harness-use is a *threat surface*, not a learning category. Kimi's specific defenses (randomized timing, encrypted segments, moving thresholds) are concrete and survive. Where Kimi overreaches: the "cryptographic enclaves" demand is over-engineered for v0 — process isolation plus mediated APIs gets 90% of the benefit. **Held**: enclaves can be a v2 hardening; not a v0 blocker.

**Kimi's "ontological fiction" framing of one-mechanism converges with my OFAT critique.** We arrive at the same place from different sides — coupling is real, one-mechanism is naive. Adopt the joint position: declared factorial ablation budgets + interaction tracking + one-causal-hypothesis (not one-component) declaration.

**DeepSeek's evaluator co-evolution claim is the sharpest single contribution.** It is what my "evaluator-capture detector" gestured at but failed to operationalize. Adopt verbatim: evaluator must be adversarially co-evolved against proposer outputs, not just frozen per epoch. My epoch-freezing primitive composes with it — freeze within an epoch, evolve between epochs. **Where DeepSeek overreaches**: "latent task validation" via real-world downstream outcomes assumes such proxies exist for harness research. Often they don't. Soften to "out-of-distribution evaluator battery with adversarially constructed tasks" — that is achievable, real-world outcome validation is aspirational.

**ChatGPT's typed telemetry, replay IDs, and leakage classes are the most directly implementable additions.** Adopt all three. Especially: every artifact carries a visibility class (`proposer-visible | aggregate-only | evaluator-only | hidden | immutable`), every event carries policy version + seed + cost + invariant status. This is the missing infrastructure under the seed's prose. ChatGPT's v0/v0.1 split is also tighter than the seed's §13 and tighter than mine. Adopt.

**Where I hold against Kimi**: Kimi calls §5 curriculum "circular" — to build harness-failure curriculum you must know harness failures. Half-true. Cold-start with hand-authored cases is unavoidable and not circular if those cases are *generators*, not the test set. My endogenous-curriculum proposal addresses this: hand-authored seed → observed-trace clustering → expanded curriculum. Kimi conflates "hard to do well" with "impossible."

**Where I hold against ChatGPT**: ChatGPT wants doctrine kept manual in v0. I argued for doctrine half-life and revalidation. These are not in conflict — *manual authorship* with *automatic revalidation scheduling* is the right combination. Adopt joint.

**What none of us addressed adequately**: the proposer itself drifts. The proposer is an LLM with biases; over epochs it develops preferences (favoring retrieval changes over prompt changes, e.g.) that are not principled. Need a **proposer audit**: track per-component change-frequency distributions and flag biased proposers. Add to v1.

**Second item none of us addressed**: doctrine inference cost. Every promoted doctrine entry adds token weight to task-agent and proposer prompts. Without an eviction policy or summarization tier, the system slowly poisons its own inference budget. Doctrine needs a working-set vs. archive split. Add to v0.

## Remaining disagreement that matters

DeepSeek argues the proposer should see only sanitized traces from a *proxy harness*, never raw evaluator traces. Kimi argues for cryptographic enclaves. ChatGPT argues for typed visibility classes on artifacts. I argue for refreshed held-out invariants per epoch. These layer rather than conflict — visibility classes are the mechanism, sanitized proxy is the policy, held-out invariants are the test, enclaves are the enforcement. All four belong. Resolved.

# Council Consensus — How to get an agent to learn its harness

## Lead claim
